title: Batch contraction + GPU slimpath orchestration for graceful OOM recovery and model fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements a coordinated runtime feature set that reduces OOM incidence and provides deterministic recovery behavior on GPU memory pressure. The feature combines: 1) adaptive batch contraction (shrinking in-flight batch windows under pressure), 2) a lightweight 'slimpath' execution mode for critical attention kernels and quantized operators, and 3) a tiered fallback orchestration that prefers intra-GPU recovery before routing to smaller/quantized model variants or CPU-hosted micro-models.

Goals:
- Prevent hard OOMs by proactively reducing working set and enabling a fast recovery path.
- Provide predictable degradation semantics (partial responses + retry) rather than opaque failures.
- Minimize customer-visible latency and cost impact by prioritizing GPU-local recoveries, then low-cost fallbacks.

Design highlights:
1) Admission & memory tickets
- Each request acquires a memory ticket estimated from sequence length, KV reservation, and requested beam/temperature. The admission controller keeps a soft budget per-GPU.
- If the ticket cannot be satisfied, the controller returns an actionable admission decision: queue, contract, or fallback. Decisions are deterministic and instrumented.

2) Continuous batch contraction
- Instead of hard batch admission limits, we implement a progressive contraction algorithm: when memory pressure > threshold A, reduce max batch window by 25%; if still above threshold B, reduce another 25%, down to a configurable min.
- Contraction is decoupled from latency SLO via an importance-aware admission: critical 'low-latency' routes can be bumped to a small reserved pool; others see increased batching delay.

3) Slimpath execution mode
- A fast-path dispatcher switches certain attention and softmax kernels to low-memory, quantization-friendly implementations at runtime when contraction alone is insufficient. These kernels prioritize memory over numeric precision (quantization + fused attention variants).
- Slimpath is applied per-layer and can be rolled back per-request if quality regressions detected.

4) Tiered fallback orchestration
- Fallback steps (in preferred order): (a) intra-GPU contraction + slimpath, (b) switch to a pinned quantized variant of the same model on-GPU, (c) route to a dedicated small micro-model on the same node (CPU/GPU hybrid), (d) route to remote dedicated capacity or queued retry.
- Each fallback step emits an event with context (reason, memory headroom, KV sizes, prior fallbacks) to build an ML signal for later policy tuning.

5) KV cache soft-eviction & reservation
- KV slots are categorized by recency/importance. On pressure, we soft-evict least-important prefixes first (marking future requests as 'cold-started').
- Requests can request 'kv-reservation' for high-value sessions which consumes extra tickets; reservations are preemptible under emergency.

Observability & metrics:
- New metrics: oom_attempts, oom_prevented_by_contraction, fallback_rate_by_step, slimpath_usage_pct, kv_eviction_rate, avg_addmitted_batch_size, p50/p90 latency during fallback, quality-regression-rate (based on prompt evaluation hooks).
- Traces must include admission decision and fallback path; logs should include per-request memory estimate and post-fallback memory headroom.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests simulate synthetic heavy-KV traffic and validate no hard OOMs in 99.9% of runs; remaining failures must be graceful (HTTP 202 + retry instructions) and documented.
- Latency p95 for non-critical routes should not regress >30% under normal load with contraction enabled.
- Quality regression (for slimpath/quantized variants) measured against control eval set must be within thresholds defined in the design doc (avg delta quality < 3% on key metrics).
- Observable fallbacks: dashboards show fallback_rate_by_step and alert if fallback_rate_by_step[0] > 0.5% for 24h on production.

Progress updates / decisions:
- 2025-11-14 (Maya Chen): Initial spike completed; prototype admission controller implemented in staging (branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2347). Key finding: naive batch window shrink causes request starvation for large-sequence jobs.
- 2025-11-18 (Luca Moreno): Added importance-aware reservations to avoid starving long-lived low-priority jobs. Updated branch to include reservation preemption logic.
- 2025-11-22 (SRE rotation): Ran 72h soak in staging with synthetic KV-heavy traffic. Result: hard OOMs reduced from 23 -> 1 per 72h, but 1 remaining OOM was caused by kernel allocation fragmentation. Kernel devs recommended a defragmentation trampoline (see ENG-59102).
- 2025-11-28 (Design review): Agreed to implement per-layer slimpath toggles rather than full-model rewrite to limit regression surface. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Batch-Contraction-Slimpath (internal).
- 2025-12-01 (QA): Added chaos tests to randomly drop KV reservations and assert fallback order is respected. Found race where concurrent soft-eviction and slimpath activation cause double-counting of freed memory; fixed by introducing a short-lived memory-epoch lock.

Implementation plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): Admission controller + continuous contraction + KV soft-eviction primitives + metrics + basic fallback orchestration to quantized pinned variant. (Canary target: runtime-1.21 canary pool).
- Phase 2 (follow-up): Slimpath per-layer kernels + micro-model routing + adaptive policy tuning via offline training.
- Phase 3: Runtime-wide rollout, integration with Console rollouts for per-tenant policies and SLOs.

Testing & canary rollout:
- Staging smoke tests: synthetic KV+long-seq workloads (scripts in /e2e/oom-sim).
- Canary 1: 1% of production requests on low-traffic region, monitor fallback_rate and user-facing errors for 48h.
- Canary 2: 10% region traffic, enable slimpath kernels for canary hosts only, monitor quality evals on synthesis prompts.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Quantization vs. latency: quantized variants reduce memory but add decode latency; choose per-route policy.
- Reservation pricing: whether to charge for kv-reservation units or make them part of enterprise SLA.
- Observability cost: increased metrics cardinality (per-request admission reasons) may raise ingestion costs; we will sample 1/1000 requests by default.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Batch-Contraction-Slimpath
- Spike branch & PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2347
- Soak run dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/oom/oom-staging-20251122

Next steps:
- Complete unit tests for admission decision matrix (assigned to Luca) by 2025-12-05.
- Wire up fallback_rate_by_step metric to Console and create an alert (oncall + SRE) before canary.
- Schedule a small customer-facing compatibility run with Solutions Engineering for two enterprise tenants that use long-sequence chat workloads (target: 2025-12-10).

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the memory-epoch lock: it's intentionally short (10ms default) to avoid throughput regressions but may impact tail latency in extreme contention. We're open to alternate approaches (lock-free counters with compare-and-swap).
- We purposely kept slimpath per-layer toggles to reduce rollout blast radius; please review the kernel API in the PR for safety knobs.

Acceptance checklist (manual):
- [ ] Unit tests for admission controller
- [ ] Integration tests for fallback ordering
- [ ] E2E soak (72h) without hard OOMs in staging
- [ ] Metrics + Console alerting wired
- [ ] PRs reviewed and merged: runtime/pull/2347, kernels/pull/91

If anything blocks progress, add it to dependencies and tag @oncall-sre.
